PullRequest.Title: Markdown editor: render Mermaid blocks like the Markdown preview
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344300

In the experimental Markdown editor, Mermaid diagrams looked different from the same diagram in the Markdown preview. They used Mermaid's default purple theme, which is hard to read in dark themes (also reported in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330433). Small diagrams were stretched to the full column width, and `markdown-mermaid.maxHeight` was ignored. The editor had its own Mermaid renderer in `markdown-language-features`, separate from the preview's in `mermaid-markdown-features`.

This PR moves the editor's Mermaid code block editor into `mermaid-markdown-features`. It is contributed through `markdown.codeBlockEditorProviders` (export API), so editor and preview share one renderer, theme mapping, and set of settings.

Demo, recorded in Code OSS from this branch. Markdown editor on the left, Markdown preview on the right:
- light, dark, and high-contrast themes
- a live edit
- `markdown-mermaid.maxHeight: "300px"` capping the initial height
- dragging the height grip past the cap

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ba9589a-0932-4ba2-a331-16e01789f621

## What changes for users

- **Theme:** diagrams use the preview's VS Code theme mapping and render again when the color theme changes.
- **Size:** diagrams render at their natural size, at most the column width and centered, like in the preview. The embedded editor's frame follows that height (`reportSize`) without scrollbars.
- **`markdown-mermaid.maxHeight`:**
  - It still defaults to empty, meaning no cap, in both the preview and the editor.
  - When set to a pixel value, the editor uses it as `maxAutomaticHeight`: it caps the initial height, and users can still drag the grip beyond it.
  - Other CSS lengths, such as `80vh`, still apply in the preview but leave the editor uncapped.
- **`markdown-mermaid.resizable`:** controls the editor's height grip.
- Setting changes apply to open Markdown editors right away.

## Changes

**mermaid-markdown-features**
- New `MermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider` (`src/markdownEditor/`). It resolves the editor page with the current `markdown-mermaid` settings, which are injected the same way as in the preview. It returns `presentation: { resizable, fullWidth, fullView, maxAutomaticHeight }` and fires `onDidChange` when settings change.
- New guest `preview-src/markdownEditor/index.ts`, built to `markdown-editor-out/`. It connects via `WebEditorClient` and reuses the preview's `loadExtensionConfig`, `VsCodeMermaidThemeTracker`, and render helpers.
  - The Markdown editor injects the theme as CSS variables plus `color-scheme`, without VS Code's body classes. The guest derives `vscode-dark`/`vscode-light` from `color-scheme` and re-renders when the injected theme changes.
  - It reports the height the diagram has at the frame's full width. Measuring the rendered height instead let a scrollbar narrow the diagram and then keep itself.
- New dependency `@vscode/web-editors`.
- `scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts` replaces the old Mermaid browser test. It hosts the guest with a real `WebEditorHost` and checks rendering, natural size, theme switching, live edits, and error recovery.

**markdown-language-features**
- Export-API code block editor providers can expose an optional `onDidChange` event. When it fires, open Markdown editors resolve that provider's blocks again.
- `maxAutomaticHeight` is accepted in the code block editor presentation (contribution schema, descriptor validation, merge).
- The Markdown editor document now uses the theme's `color-scheme`. Before, embedded frames had `color-scheme: dark` in dark themes while the editor document was `normal`, so Chromium painted an opaque backdrop behind every embedded editor. That showed as a dark box behind Mermaid diagrams and other embedded editors.
- Removed the built-in Mermaid renderer (`markdown-editor-src/mermaid/`), its build plugin and test, and the `mermaid` dependency.
- Updated `@vscode/markdown-editor` from 0.0.2-136 to 0.0.2-147. This brings the embedded editor chrome from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/392 (hover outline, toolbar, snapping grips, `maxAutomaticHeight`) and the presentation protocol from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/396.

## Validation

- `npm run test-extension -- -l markdown-language-features`: 192 passing. This includes new tests for `maxAutomaticHeight` validation and presentation merging.
- `node --test scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts` in `mermaid-markdown-features` passes.
- Typecheck of both extensions (including `tsconfig.markdownEditor.json` and `preview-src`), ESLint, hygiene, and `check-markdown-editor-package-json` all pass.
- Manual check in Code OSS with the published 0.0.2-147 package, comparing the editor and preview side by side:
  - Light Modern, Dark Modern, and Default High Contrast.
  - Live theme switching.
  - Setting `maxHeight` while the editor is open.
  - Resizing past the cap.
  - Frame heights equal the diagram heights, with no stray scrollbars.

Pan and zoom in the editor, as toolbar actions, are a later step.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added event handler directly invokes a loader that awaits an uncached filesystem read for every static contribution. Per-panel subscriptions establish M*S reads without relying on unavailable SDK internals; file sizes and remote latency are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem reads and associated IPC, full HTML byte decoding, and provider-definition payloads.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each settings event causes M open panels to issue S static-provider reads each: M*S calls and M times the combined HTML bytes. Panels run concurrently; reads within each panel are sequential and are not coalesced across panels.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive filesystem/IPC work and delayed settings application behind unrelated resource reads.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Mermaid setting changes did not trigger the Markdown editor's provider loader. Static HTML was read during editor initialization or contribution/resource invalidation, not unrelated Mermaid configuration changes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Provider onDidChange events are forwarded without provider identity to a global event. Every open Markdown panel responds by clearing all resolved descriptors and loading all provider definitions, including unrelated static HTML.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 705-707 invoke refreshCodeBlockEditorProviders(false, true) for every panel. That function clears all resolved caches and awaits #loadCodeBlockEditorProviders, whose contribution loop at lines 790-803 reads every static provider. Added lines 935-936 discard the identity of the provider that changed.
Findings.Title: Scope refreshes to the provider that changed
Findings.Impact: After resolving a Mermaid editor, changing a Mermaid setting with M Markdown panels open causes M*S unrelated HTML reads for S installed static providers, even when their blocks are absent. Applying the setting waits behind S sequential reads per panel, potentially over a remote extension filesystem.
Findings.Evidence: MermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider fires on markdown-mermaid setting changes at mermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider.ts:25-28. Each open panel subscribes to the global event. #loadCodeBlockEditorProviders awaits vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(provider.source.resource) inside its loop, with no cache or in-flight joining. Static providers are supported by both the contribution schema and legacy markdown.codeBlockEditors. The renderer notification waits for all these reads.
Findings.Recommendation: Carry the changed provider ID through the event, invalidate only its descriptors, and refresh it without reloading unchanged static contributions. Retain full reloads for contribution/resource changes.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The configuration serializer includes preview-only keys, the new runtime key hashes that serialization, and the documented iframe contract prohibits reuse across different keys. The guest never consumes these keys. Exact recreated-frame counts depend on virtualization, so the finding is limited to instantiated frames rather than every document block.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Iframe/guest-runtime creation, Mermaid initialization, diagram parsing, SVG layout, and DOM reconstruction.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Work scales with the number of instantiated Mermaid frames refreshed across open panels and each diagram's complexity, not all fenced blocks. Warm script caches can reduce transferred bytes but do not eliminate fresh guest initialization and rendering.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Avoidable diagram redraw latency and renderer CPU/allocation pressure on preview-only configuration changes.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The built-in Mermaid provider used the constant runtimeKey vscode.markdown.mermaid, and changing preview controls or mouse-navigation settings did not refresh or reconstruct the Markdown editor's Mermaid frames.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The provider hashes the entire HTML, including all shared preview settings, into the runtime key. Its configuration listener also fires for preview-only changes, so otherwise compatible editor frames receive an incompatible runtime identity.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 40 derives runtimeKey from hashString(html); line 35 builds that HTML with renderMermaidConfigSpan(). The added listener at lines 25–28 fires for any markdown-mermaid configuration change. Previously the deleted mermaidProvider.ts:13 used a constant runtime key.
Findings.Title: Exclude preview-only settings from the Mermaid runtime key
Findings.Impact: Changing controls.show or mouseNavigation.enabled for the preview unnecessarily reconstructs instantiated Mermaid frames in open Markdown editors and redraws unchanged diagrams. With several visible, complex diagrams this adds avoidable rendering latency and CPU work to a setting change that has no editor effect.
Findings.Evidence: src/markdownMermaid/config.ts:33–43 serializes clickDrag (mouseNavigation.enabled) and showControls (controls.show) along with rendering settings. Neither value is read by preview-src/markdownEditor/index.ts or buildMermaidConfig, and neither affects the provider's presentation. Nevertheless either changes the hashed HTML. markdown-language-features/schemas/package.schema.json:107 documents that only equal runtime keys may reuse an iframe. Each replacement guest runs main(), registers addons/connects, and performs a fresh Mermaid parse/render through renderMermaidBlocksInElement.
Findings.Recommendation: Filter onDidChange to settings actually consumed by the Markdown editor, and exclude preview-only fields from its serialized runtime configuration/key. Preserve runtime invalidation for genuine rendering-setting changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Markdown editor, with or without Mermaid blocks, including several diagrams in view.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor initializes independently of the asynchronous provider-definition load. A Mermaid diagram requires provider resolution, guest module loading, addon registration, WebEditorClient connection, and parsing/rendering before its SVG and automatic height appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: M*S reads during initial panel loading; export-API contributions add no HTML read here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same loader already read all installed static contributions on panel initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider definitions wait for S sequential reads per panel; main editor initialization does not await them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Mermaid descriptors through the extension-host RPC and activate/get the extension provider on a cold miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Adapter requests cross RPC; actual provider resolution coalesces to one per provider/document/language key, with one cached provider API per contribution. Mermaid returns inline small HTML and no content.uri read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The built-in provider resolved locally using a cached dynamic import of its inline Mermaid HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before a Mermaid guest can be created; not required for plain Markdown editing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load external index.js and its static/dynamic module dependencies through the webview resource service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requested module set K per new guest realm; browser transport reuse can group requests. Warm service-worker cache entries supply bytes after ETag validation. Icon packs have lazy import loaders, not unconditional per-icon requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor's Mermaid HTML contained a bundled inline IIFE rather than external module requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Guest startup and selected diagram rendering await required modules.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M open panels, S installed static providers, D distinct documents requesting Mermaid, V instantiated Mermaid frames, and K modules actually loaded by each diagram type. Virtualization means V is not the total fenced-block count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Static reads are sequential within each panel and parallel across panels. Guests are virtualized by the external adapter. Each guest awaits addon registration then connection. Electron webview resource responses have a shared 32-body semaphore; web does not use that limiter. External adapter internals were unavailable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider APIs and resolved descriptor promises coalesce cold requests; descriptor successes are keyed by provider/document/language, while unsuccessful descriptors are removed. Modules are reusable through browser/resource caching, but each iframe has its own initialized guest realm. LazyCodeBlockEditorFactory still defers adapter loading until code blocks are encountered.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in source-level boundary placement and descriptor cache keys; limited confidence in exact module-request grouping or external adapter scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime timings or bundle sizes were measured. The upgraded external markdown-editor package and Mermaid implementation were not available through repository-file reads, so exact virtualization limits and parser internals could not be inspected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional startup finding: the provider migration adds small descriptor RPC and external resources but also replaces large inline renderer HTML, and available evidence does not establish a net startup regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live Mermaid source edits, parse-error recovery, and VS Code color-theme switches.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each content change starts a guest render. The previous SVG remains displayed while staging is rendered. The latest non-aborted result replaces it and reports size. Color-theme changes recompute the theme fingerprint and render when it changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive source updates and report changed content height over the embedded-editor protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Source updates follow host content notifications; height reports only occur when the positive rounded height changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted Mermaid guest also used WebEditorClient content notifications and deduplicated height reports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Source delivery precedes rendering; size reports affect the containing frame's layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load diagram-type or icon-pack modules when needed by a new diagram type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only requested module/pack keys, with warm module caches in each realm and resource-cache ETag behavior across realms; not one request per node/icon.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The built-in IIFE bundled Mermaid dependencies; it did not register these shared icon/addon loaders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A render may await a newly required module.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Content-change frequency, source length/diagram complexity, and instantiated guests receiving a theme update, including any pooled guests whose head theme CSS is updated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single guest can have overlapping async render attempts; only the latest is committed. Within each attempt parse is awaited before render. Multiple guests can render concurrently; exact Mermaid queue behavior is outside the available repository source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme variables are memoized until refresh, and unchanged fingerprints suppress theme renders. No rendered-SVG cache is introduced. Each render aborts its predecessor; shared rendering checks abortion after parse and render. These checks do not pass cancellation into Mermaid itself.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in event-to-render paths, cancellation checkpoints, and theme fingerprint suppression; insufficient evidence for a separately reportable redundant-parse or eager-addon mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional parsing and addon-loading candidates require unavailable dependency internals to rule out internal caching/lazy registration. No latency measurements exist. Pooled-frame population is also external.
Scenarios.Verdict: Required theme rerendering and improved staging/error handling do not alone establish a regression. Dependency-dependent duplicate parsing, tooltip retention, and eager addon loading were not reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change Mermaid settings while multiple Markdown editors and unrelated code-block providers are open.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider event is broadcast to every open panel. Each refresh clears all resolved descriptors, awaits loading all definitions, then notifies its renderer. Mermaid settings cannot take effect through that refresh until unrelated static reads finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reread every static provider's unchanged HTML on one provider's configuration event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly M*S calls per event through this loader, with M*B decoded bytes. No static-resource cache or cross-panel joining is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The filesystem loader existed, but Mermaid setting changes did not invoke it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each panel's settings refresh awaits its S reads serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish all provider definitions to each ready panel; read resources through a local provider shortcut or main-thread filesystem RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One all-definitions notification per ready panel after a current refresh. Filesystem requests follow the M*S reads; local-provider shortcut paths may avoid the readFile RPC but still perform the read and safe copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No such provider notification or resource reads were issued by the Markdown editor on Mermaid setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The renderer refresh is delayed until definitions are reloaded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read URI-backed dynamic-provider HTML after global descriptor-cache invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On subsequent resolution, one read per effective provider/document/language cache miss, not per fenced block. For example, the repository checkbox-count provider returns editor/index.html as content.uri.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Previously warm unrelated descriptors stayed cached on Mermaid setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Those unrelated descriptors must be read again before their resolution completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M open Markdown panels, S installed static providers, the combined static HTML byte size B, and effective dynamic provider/document/language keys subsequently requested. Once the Mermaid API has been resolved, its configuration listener remains available even for panels without Mermaid blocks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: M panels refresh concurrently; S static reads are sequential in each panel. contributionUpdate suppresses obsolete publication but does not cancel issued filesystem reads. No shared loader limiter/coalescer is present.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new event retains provider API caches but unconditionally clears all descriptor/resource caches. Static reads have no positive/negative cache or in-flight coalescing here. Dynamic descriptor requests still coalesce by provider/document/language after invalidation. Repeated events invalidate again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added handler, per-panel subscription ownership, unconditional static loop, and pre/post event behavior are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed static-provider counts and HTML sizes vary; remote extension resources can be slower. S can be zero, so the unconditional static-file impact is conditional on installed static/legacy providers. Exact downstream adapter refresh behavior is external.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported boundary-fanout finding at markdownEditorProvider.ts:706. The report uses M*S installed static contributions rather than incorrectly claiming per-diagram filesystem calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change preview-only controls.show or mouseNavigation.enabled with Mermaid diagrams instantiated in Markdown editors.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared config span changes, yielding a different runtime key. Refreshed Mermaid descriptors cannot reuse compatible old iframe runtimes, so replacement guests load/connect/initialize and render unchanged diagrams.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload guest modules for replacement iframe realms through the webview resource loader.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Required module set per recreated realm; warm resource caches and browser request grouping reduce transferred bytes. Service-worker hits still use ETag validation if the fetch reaches that service worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These preview-only settings did not recreate built-in editor Mermaid runtimes or issue associated module loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replacement guest rendering requires its modules, protocol connection, and initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect each replacement guest to its parent and report the newly rendered size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection per recreated guest and deduplicated height reports within that fresh guest lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing Mermaid guest connections survived these preview-only setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection precedes the initial content render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V instantiated Mermaid frames that are refreshed, their diagram complexity, and preview-setting-change frequency. Counts are not total document blocks because frames are virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replacement guests can initialize/render independently, constrained by adapter virtualization and the Electron resource-response limiter rather than a proven global Mermaid render limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new runtime identity hashes all shared settings, including clickDrag and showControls that neither the editor guest nor presentation consumes. Thus warm compatible runtimes are deliberately made ineligible for reuse despite unchanged editor rendering. Script-byte caches cannot prevent repeated guest initialization and SVG rendering.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serializer fields, whole-HTML hash, broad configuration event, absence of editor consumers for these two fields, and iframe reuse contract are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame counts and diagram-render duration are unmeasured; the external adapter implementation was unavailable. The documented equal-runtime-key reuse contract establishes incompatibility independently of those magnitudes.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported cache-lifecycle finding at mermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider.ts:40. It is distinct from global provider invalidation: even a correctly targeted refresh would still unnecessarily invalidate Mermaid runtimes for preview-only settings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, scroll, full-width/full-view presentation, and editor/extension disposal.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver computes natural height from SVG aspect ratio and frame width, reporting only changed positive heights. Resize does not invoke Mermaid rendering. On pagehide the guest aborts rendering and disconnects both observers, content subscription, and client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Report automatic frame height to the host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one report per distinct rounded positive height per guest, with no diagram rerender on size observation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old guest observed its container and used the same reported-height deduplication pattern.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Affects frame sizing but not source-edit completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Instantiated frames and resize frequency; lifecycle ownership is per guest, per panel listener, and per cached provider API.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser observer callbacks run on the guest UI thread. No changed subprocess/filesystem/database/network operations occur during the ordinary resize calculation or explicit guest cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current SVG survives presentation changes within a compatible runtime; currentRender is replaced rather than retained in a collection. Provider API listeners are disposed on cache clearing and extension-provider disposal, and per-panel global-event listeners are disposed when the panel closes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High in the visible deduplication and cleanup ownership; limited in external host sizing internals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host presentation/virtualization implementation belongs to the upgraded package and could not be read. Browser tests provide behavioral context, not performance measurements.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence sizing or retention regression. The natural-height formula avoids dependence on the scrollbar-narrowed diagram, and visible cleanup retains the necessary disposal handles.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing Markdown preview, notebook, and chat Mermaid rendering, plus extension activation and build changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing preview/notebook/chat rendering paths remain in their existing bundles. The new extension provider adds only an event emitter/configuration listener during activation; it does not open diagrams or read resources eagerly. New build work is off product runtime critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute markdown.preview.refresh and, for language-setting changes, markdown.api.reloadPlugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing command invocations per matching configuration event; no added command loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing preview refresh path, independent of the new editor provider event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the new standalone editor bundle while removing the old inline Mermaid bundling plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional mermaid extension build entrypoint and one removed markdown-language extension Mermaid build plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Mermaid was bundled into inline HTML by the Markdown editor build rather than the mermaid extension's separate output directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build-time only, not ordinary application startup/rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new provider instance per extension activation and one new build entrypoint; existing preview configuration-change frequency is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The added build entrypoint joins the existing Promise.all build batch. Runtime activation registrations are bounded; no new subprocess or database calls were found in that path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing shared preview rendering/theme/config state is unchanged. The new provider owns a single configuration listener and disposes it with its event emitter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that visible preview/chat runtime work is preserved and added provider activation is bounded; insufficient evidence to classify dependency/build changes as a regression fix.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dependency-version implementation changes and output bundle sizes could not be evaluated without package sources/build output. Supporting performance-guide output was truncated by the read tool.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding or regression-fix learning signal. Removing duplicate inline renderer code may reduce work, but a concrete old regression and introducing provenance were not established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 26 changed files and every diff page, including all paginated lockfile sections. Submitted two accepted findings: unscoped provider-event filesystem fan-out (M*S installed static providers across panels) and incompatible runtime keys for unused preview-only settings (instantiated frames, not total blocks). Investigated rendering, caches/coalescing, external resource loading/ETag validation, actual resource concurrency, sizing, activation, and disposal. No code was changed or executed. Unavailable dependency implementations and truncated supporting guide output limit dependency-internal conclusions; no qualifying regression-fix provenance was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
